edges.description: Absent surface TIM-3 removes an inhibitory input on macrophages and dendritic cells, lowering the threshold for innate activation.
Sustained innate activation escalates into the systemic macrophage activation syndrome recognised clinically as HLH.
The chronic inflammatory milieu is the proposed context in which a cytotoxic T-cell clone emerges and is sustained.
The expanded cytotoxic clone encircles and kills individual adipocytes within the fat lobule.
Destructive lobular panniculitis is what the patient feels and the clinician sees as nodules and plaques.
Systemic macrophage activation is the mechanism behind the clinical HLH syndrome.

nodes.description: The histologic hallmark of the disease: atypical cytotoxic lymphocytes surround individual adipocytes in a lace-like pattern within a lobular panniculitis, with karyorrhexis and fat necrosis and without epidermal involvement. Adipocyte death is the direct tissue-level readout of T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity in this compartment.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic profiles of subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and clinicopathological impact of HAVCR2 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Histopathologically, SPTCL is characterized by CD8-positive T cells infiltrating into subcutaneous adipose tissue, with rimmed individual fat cells in a lace-like pattern.

evidence.reference_title: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma: Clinical features, therapeutic approach, and outcome in a case series of 16 patients.
evidence.snippet: Histopathology typically showed a lobular panniculitis with individual adipocytes surrounded by atypical lymphocytes, usually with a CD3+, CD4-, CD8+, CD56-, TIA1 cytotoxic granule associated RNA binding protein 1-positive phenotype and high proliferation rate.

nodes.description: A clonal population of CD3-positive, CD4-negative, CD8-positive, CD56-negative, betaF1-positive cytotoxic T cells expands and homes to subcutaneous fat. Cooperating somatic mutations in epigenetic regulators and signal transducers accompany the germline lesion. In HAVCR2 p.Tyr82Cys tumours the transcriptional program is enriched for IL6-JAK-STAT3 and for TNF signalling via NF-kappaB, which is the stated rationale for JAK inhibition.

biological_processes: cell surface receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT

evidence.reference_title: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma: definition, classification, and prognostic factors: an EORTC Cutaneous Lymphoma Group Study of 83 cases.
evidence.snippet: SPTL-ABs were generally confined to the subcutis, had a CD4-, CD8+, CD56-, betaF1+ phenotype, were uncommonly associated with a hemophagocytic syndrome (HPS; 17%), and had a favorable prognosis (5-year overall survival [OS]: 82%).

evidence.reference_title: Genetic profiles of subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and clinicopathological impact of HAVCR2 mutations.
evidence.snippet: At the gene expression level, HAVCR2Y82C SPTCLs were enriched in genes involved in IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling and in tumor necrosis factor-α signaling via NF-κB.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent germline mutations of HAVCR2 in sporadic subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma.
evidence.snippet: SPTCL cells also harbored somatic mutations (6.2 per patient) that are frequently identified in genes associated with epigenetic regulation and signal transduction.

nodes.description: Systemic corticosteroids alone or combined with low-dose methotrexate or cyclosporine A. This is now the usual first-line choice for uncomplicated cutaneous disease, and gives high complete response rates without the toxicity of anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Corticosteroid monotherapy relapses more often than corticosteroids combined with another immunoregulatory agent.

evidence.reference_title: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma: Clinical features, therapeutic approach, and outcome in a case series of 16 patients.
evidence.snippet: Oral steroids alone or in combination with low-dose methotrexate or cyclosporine A were the most common initial treatment, achieving a complete response in 85% of the treated patients.

evidence.reference_title: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma associated with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis: a systematic review of 63 patients reported in the literature.
evidence.snippet: The corticosteroid monotherapy experienced a higher recurrence rate than the corticosteroids plus other immunoregulatory agents therapy (66.7 vs. 0.0%, p = 0.029).

nodes.description: Germline missense variants in HAVCR2 substitute conserved residues in the extracellular immunoglobulin variable-like domain of TIM-3. The variant proteins misfold and never reach the plasma membrane, so the inhibitory receptor is functionally absent from the surface of T cells and of the myeloid cells that normally use it to damp innate activation. The geographic split between the two commonest alleles - p.Tyr82Cys on an East Asian and Polynesian founder haplotype, p.Ile97Met in European-ancestry patients - is a strong argument that these are ancestral, not somatic, lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Germline HAVCR2 mutations altering TIM-3 characterize subcutaneous panniculitis-like T cell lymphomas with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytic syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We identify in ~60% of SPTCL cases germline, loss-of-function, missense variants altering highly conserved residues of TIM-3, c.245A>G (p.Tyr82Cys) and c.291A>G (p.Ile97Met), each with specific geographic distribution.

evidence.reference_title: Germline HAVCR2 mutations altering TIM-3 characterize subcutaneous panniculitis-like T cell lymphomas with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytic syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Both variants induce protein misfolding and abrogate TIM-3's plasma membrane expression, leading to persistent immune activation and increased production of inflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor-α and interleukin-1β, promoting HLH and SPTCL.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent germline mutations of HAVCR2 in sporadic subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma.
evidence.snippet: Ten patients harbored homozygous p.Y82C mutations, and 1 showed compound heterozygous mutations (p.Y82C and p.T101I).

genetic_context.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous germline missense alleles; the commonest genotype reported is homozygous p.Tyr82Cys.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent germline mutations of HAVCR2 in sporadic subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma.
evidence.snippet: Consistent with a recent report, germline mutations in HAVCR2, encoding T-cell immunoglobulin mucin 3 (TIM3), were identified in 11 of 13 (85%) cases.

meta.frequency: Reported in roughly 50% to 86% of patients depending on cohort ancestry and on whether the series is enriched for paediatric or HLH-complicated disease.

nodes.description: The commonest reported allele, carried on a probable founder chromosome in patients of East Asian and Polynesian ancestry. Causes TIM-3 misfolding and loss of plasma membrane expression.

evidence.reference_title: Germline HAVCR2 mutations altering TIM-3 characterize subcutaneous panniculitis-like T cell lymphomas with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytic syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The variant encoding p.Tyr82Cys TIM-3 occurs on a potential founder chromosome in patients with East Asian and Polynesian ancestry, while p.Ile97Met TIM-3 occurs in patients with European ancestry.

nodes.description: The predominant allele in patients of European ancestry, with the same misfolding and trafficking defect as p.Tyr82Cys.

evidence.reference_title: Germline HAVCR2 mutations altering TIM-3 characterize subcutaneous panniculitis-like T cell lymphomas with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytic syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We identify in ~60% of SPTCL cases germline, loss-of-function, missense variants altering highly conserved residues of TIM-3, c.245A>G (p.Tyr82Cys) and c.291A>G (p.Ile97Met), each with specific geographic distribution.

nodes.description: A third recurrent allele, reported in compound heterozygosity with p.Tyr82Cys.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent germline mutations of HAVCR2 in sporadic subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma.
evidence.snippet: Ten patients harbored homozygous p.Y82C mutations, and 1 showed compound heterozygous mutations (p.Y82C and p.T101I).

nodes.description: In a substantial minority of patients the innate activation described above escalates into full hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, with activated macrophages engulfing blood cells in marrow, spleen and liver and a systemic cytokine excess producing fever, cytopenias, hyperferritinaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia and hypofibrinogenaemia. HLH risk tracks HAVCR2 genotype dose and is higher in children and in males.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic profiles of subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and clinicopathological impact of HAVCR2 mutations.
evidence.snippet: HAVCR2Y82C was associated with younger age (P = .001), development of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-like systemic illness (P < .001), and short relapse-free survival (RFS) (P = .023).

evidence.reference_title: Germline HAVCR2 mutations and their relation to the clinical spectrum of subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
evidence.snippet: Homozygous HAVCR2Y82C mutation was more common in the presence of HLH compared with the absence (75.0% vs. 44.4%; P=0.02).

nodes.description: A JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor. Its use follows directly from the mechanism: TIM-3 loss drives cytokine-mediated inflammation and HAVCR2-mutant tumours are transcriptionally enriched for IL6-JAK-STAT3 signalling. Reported responses in HAVCR2-mutant children have been rapid and durable after corticosteroids, other immunosuppressants and chemotherapy had all failed.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of ruxolitinib for HAVCR2 mutation-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and panniculitis manifestations in children.
evidence.snippet: All patients initially received corticosteroids, immunosuppressants or chemotherapy, achieving unfavourable responses. Strikingly, they responded well to ruxolitinib targeting inflammatory cytokines, allowing rapid disease resolution and/or long-term maintenance of remission.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of ruxolitinib in subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
evidence.snippet: First evidence of ruxolitinib efficacy for subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

nodes.description: With TIM-3 missing from the cell surface, myeloid cells sustain innate signalling that would normally be terminated. The measured consequence in patient material is persistent immune activation with excess production of inflammatory cytokines, notably TNF and interleukin-1 beta. Inflammasome assembly is the proposed proximal route to interleukin-1 family cytokine release; that step is inferred from TIM-3 biology rather than demonstrated directly in SPTCL tissue, and is recorded here at lower confidence than the cytokine measurements themselves.

evidence.reference_title: Germline HAVCR2 mutations altering TIM-3 characterize subcutaneous panniculitis-like T cell lymphomas with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytic syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Both variants induce protein misfolding and abrogate TIM-3's plasma membrane expression, leading to persistent immune activation and increased production of inflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor-α and interleukin-1β, promoting HLH and SPTCL.

evidence.reference_title: Germline HAVCR2 mutations and their relation to the clinical spectrum of subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
evidence.snippet: These mutations result in misfolding of T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain containing-3 (TIM-3) protein, leading to persistent immune activation and cytokine release, which are responsible for the pathogenesis of HLH.
